Create isopleths from utilisation distributions

Source: R/hr_tt_ud_iso.R
hr_tt_ud_iso.Rd

This method can be applied to a whole tibble of UDs, or to an individual UD.

Usage

hr_tt_ud_iso(x, levels = c(0.5, 0.95), ci_level = 0.95)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_df'
hr_tt_ud_iso(x, levels = c(0.5, 0.95), ci_level = 0.95)

# S3 method for class 'SpatRaster'
hr_tt_ud_iso(x, levels = c(0.5, 0.95), ci_level = 0.95)

Arguments

x

either a tibble of class hr_tt_ud_tbl, as created by hr_tt_kde(), or a SpatRaster object from the ud column of a hr_tt_ud_tbl tibble.

levels

numeric vector of isopleth levels to create. Default is c(0.50, 0.95), which will create 50% and 95% isopleths. Levels should be between 0 and 1.

ci_level

The confidence level of the confidence intervals of the areas of the isopleths, which are computed for the UDs estimated with ctmm (i.e. a table with a ud_ctmm column, as returned by hr_tt_akde() and hr_tt_akde_pop()); it is ignored for other UDs. Default is 0.95.

Value

If x is a SpatRaster, an sf object with one row per level and columns level, area (the area of the isopleth) and geometry (a MULTIPOLYGON for the isopleth). If x is a tibble, an sf tibble of class hr_tt_poly_tbl with the columns of x (except ud and ud_ctmm) and, for each UD, one row per level with these three columns. For the UDs estimated with ctmm, the columns area_low and area_high (the confidence interval of the home range area at each level, as estimated by ctmm) are added after area (in a table that combines them with other UDs, e.g. from hr_tt_kde(), the other UDs get NA).

See also

Other home_range: hr_tt_ud_sum()

Examples

example_kde <- hr_tt_kde(example_tt)
example_iso <- hr_tt_ud_iso(example_kde)
example_iso
#> Simple feature collection with 6 features and 10 fields
#> Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -7.665867 ymin: -4.377112 xmax: 7.900379 ymax: 5.851994
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#> # A tibble: 6 × 11
#>   track_id method     h  xmin  ymin  xmax  ymax   res level          area
#> * <chr>    <chr>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>         [m^2]
#> 1 a        kde     1.06 -16.5 -7.42  16.6  9.54 0.737  0.5  169367467153.
#> 2 a        kde     1.06 -16.5 -7.42  16.6  9.54 0.737  0.95 686843555092.
#> 3 b        kde     1.06 -16.5 -7.42  16.6  9.54 0.737  0.5   99573159553.
#> 4 b        kde     1.06 -16.5 -7.42  16.6  9.54 0.737  0.95 436476848051.
#> 5 c        kde     1.06 -16.5 -7.42  16.6  9.54 0.737  0.5  118862309232.
#> 6 c        kde     1.06 -16.5 -7.42  16.6  9.54 0.737  0.95 530109135082.
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: geometry <MULTIPOLYGON [°]>

# now plot the isopleths
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(example_iso) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = track_id), alpha = 0.7)
